 Dated This The 30 th Day Of January 2024 
 Present: Smt. Kusuma. V.
 Metropolitan Magistrate,
 Traffic Court-III, Bengaluru. 
 Crl. Misc. No. 20/2023
Petitioners : Smt. K. Jayalakshmi,
 W/o Shanmukhappa. H.B.
 Aged about 65 Yrs,
 R/at No.8, 1st Main,
 1st Cross, Bagalagunte,
 Nagasandra,
 Bengaluru-73.
 (By Sri. H.C.R. Adv.)
 V/s. 
Respondent : Shanmukhappa. H.B.
 S/o Bheemappa,
 Aged 70 Yrs,
 R/at Hindaskatte Village,
 Nalkunda Post,
 Mayakonda Hobli,
 Davanagere Taluk & District. 
 (Ex-parte)
 2  C.Misc. 20/2023  ORDERS ON MAIN PETITION  1. This is petition filed by the petitioner U/sec. 12 of Protection Of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005. 
 2. By filing this petition the petitioner has sought Jayalakshmi. K vs Shanmukhappa. H B on 30 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114123177/
1 various reliefs fallen U/sec. 18, 19, 20 & 22 of PWDV Act- 2005. 
 3. The format as required under the DV Act is duly filled up and the same is presented by the petitioner along with the affidavit. In the required format, the detail of the petitioners' case cannot be made out, the same can be gone through in the evidence let in by the petitioner. Hence,
before considering the reliefs sought for, it becomes just and necessary to look into the case of the petitioner. 
 4. The petitioner submits that the petitioner and the respondent marriage was celebrated on 28.5.1978 at Dondi Kalyan Mantapa, Bengaluru. Out of the said wedlock,
between the petitioner and the respondent two children were born one daughter namely Meenakshi, Son namely  3  C.Misc. 20/2023 Jayaram. After two children were born, the petitioner and the respondent made family planning by medical treatment to the petitioner. Unfortunately, the son Jayaram was suffering from Heart problem at the age 6 yrs and finally the said son was died. 
 5. The petitioner further submits that after the death of said petitioner's son, the attitude of the respondent totally changed, the respondent used to abuse in filthy language and assaulting the petitioner for the reasons best known to Jayalakshmi. K vs Shanmukhappa. H B on 30 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114123177/
2 him. After that, the respondent failed to provide provision and made the petitioner and her daughter to live without food. 
 6. The petitioner further submits that in the month of May, 1991, the respondent brought the girl named Sudha,
resident of Anaberu village, Davanagere taluk, she started to staying in the house and the respondent started illegal relationship with said Sudha. The respondent totally ignored and deserted the petitioner and stopped his  4  C.Misc. 20/2023 relationship with the petitioner by mentally and physically,
the respondent not even mind to speak with the petitioner.
The respondent stopped the education of the petitioner's daughter Meenakshi, later the respondent suddenly arranged the marriage of Meenakshi with the brother of Sudha, the petitioner tried to stop the marriage in all means but all went in vain, finally minor daughter marriage was performed by the respondent. After this, second wife of respondent gave birth to daughter and son named as Soumya and Yeshwanth. The respondent gave good education to second wife children as the said Soumya completed BE, Engineering and Yeshwanth completed Diploma. 
 7. The petitioner further submits that the respondent never reciprocated towards the petitioner and his behaviour Jayalakshmi. K vs Shanmukhappa. H B on 30 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114123177/
3 remained the same and respondent did not perform his matrimonial obligations. The petitioner left the matrimonial house 15 yrs back during December 2007. 
 5  C.Misc. 20/2023  8. The petitioner further submits that in the year 1996,
the respondent was purchased 30 x 40 ft site from Ramachandraiah and Lakshmamma and constructed one ground floored house vide door No. 348, situated at Babanna Layout, Mallasandra, Bengaluru. Later in the year 2000, the respondent constructed the first and second floored house, in total 9 houses, one house kept for self and 8 houses left for public on rent basis. In the year 1996 made power of attorney in favour of the petitioner, but not made the sale deed. In the year 2011, the said house sale deed was registered in the name of Sudha. 
 9. The petitioner further submits that respondent was working as Electrician at Tata Global Beveranges Ltd., at Malonagattihalli village, Tumkur Road, Bengaluru as Supervisor and Production Manager earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- and earning house rent of Rs.20,000/- per month. The petitioner is in requirement of Rs.10,000/- per month as on date of provision ratings. It is submitted that the respondent was working at TATA Ltd., and was drawing  6  C.Misc. 20/2023 a very good salary at the time of retirement, he got Jayalakshmi. K vs Shanmukhappa. H B on 30 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114123177/
4 handsome retirement benefits, however, out of his salary and retirement benefit, he has purchased the immovable properties in the name of his second wife. Hence, prays to allow the petition. 
 10. On service of notice, the respondent has not appeared before court. Hence, the respondent was placed ex-parte on 13.06.2023. 
 11. Keeping in mind the evidence given by the petitioner it becomes just and necessary to look into whether the orders required by the petitioner various reliefs which are fallen U/sec. 18, 19, 20 and 22 of DV Act can be granted. 
 12. The petitioner in support of her case has got examined herself as PW.1 and got exhibited documents as Exs. P.1 to 4 . Ex.P.1 is certified copy of sale deed dtd:
25.11.2002, Ex.P.2 is notarized copy of salary slip of respondent, Ex.P.3 is notarized copy of adhar card and Ex.P.4 is ration card. 
 7  C.Misc. 20/2023  13. Heard arguments from counsel for the petitioner. 
Perused the documents. 
 14. The points that arise for consideration are:- 
 1. Whether the petitioner is entitled for  the Protection Orders as contemplated  under Sec.18 of DV Act?
 2.Whether the petitioner is entitled for Jayalakshmi. K vs Shanmukhappa. H B on 30 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114123177/
5  residential relief as contemplated under Sec.19 of DV Act? 
 3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for  monetary relief as contemplated under Sec.20 of DV Act? 
 4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for  compensation relief as contemplated  under Sec.22 of DV Act?
 5. What order?
 15. The findings to the above points are as follows:-
 Point Nos.1 to 4: In the Negative  Point No.5: As per Final Order, for the  following:-
 R EAS O N S  16. Reasoning on Point No.1 to 4: Since these points are interconnected with each other and requires common  8  C.Misc. 20/2023 appreciation of evidence, hence to avoid repetition of facts all the points are taken together for common consideration.
 17. The case of the petitioner is that the respondent has given mental and physical harassment by neglecting the petitioner and her daughter. 
 18. As per the provisions of Sec.18 of DV Act. As per this section, the Magistrate may, after giving the petitioner and the respondent an opportunity of being heard and on being prima-facie satisfied that domestic violence has taken place or is likely to take place, pass a protection order in favour of the petitioner and prohibit the respondent from committing such domestic violence. 
Jayalakshmi. K vs Shanmukhappa. H B on 30 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114123177/
6  19. In the affidavit filed by the petitioner along with petition she has stated that the averments made in the petition are all true and correct. The petitioner has stated that she was subjected to verbal, physical, mental and emotional abuse and she was also subjected to economic violence by not providing money for maintaining herself and  9  C.Misc. 20/2023 her daughter and the respondent was not providing food,
cloths, for herself and her daughter and he had relationship with one Sudha and said Sudha gave birth to two children.
Thereafter, the respondent totally neglected the petitioner and her daughter. Therefore, the petitioner was forced to leave the matrimonial house by the respondent about 15 yrs back ie., on December 2007. 
 20 . Further on perusal of the petition, the main contention of the petitioner the respondent harassed her and her daughter mentally and physically by not providing basic necessities to them. Further, the respondent had given good education to their children who were born through one Sudha. But, the respondent has not given proper education to the daughter of the petitioner namely Meenakshi. 
Thereafter, the respondent always avoided the petitioner mentally and physically. For this reason, the petitioner herself has left the matrimonial home in the year December 2007. No where in the petition, the petitioner has stated  10 Jayalakshmi. K vs Shanmukhappa. H B on 30 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114123177/
7  C.Misc. 20/2023 regarding domestic violence caused by the respondent towards her and her daughter. On the other hand, after issuance of notice, the said notice was served on respondent, but he has not received the same and he was not appeared before court. Hence he placed ex-parte.
 21. No doubt, as per Sec.3 of DV Act, if at all the respondent commits any domestic violence as above pleaded is fully established by the petitioner then definitely the petitioner will be entitled for an order of protection under Sec.18 and for residential orders as per Sec.18 of DV Act and mandatory reliefs as contemplated under Sec.20 of the Act. 
 22 . In the case on hand, it is the case of the petitioner that she is residing along with the respondent after the marriage in the shared house, wherein the respondent has given mental and physical torture by not providing basic necessities to the petitioner and her daughter. Here the petitioner has prayed relief of alternative accommodation. In this case, the petitioner has not proved the allegations made  11  C.Misc. 20/2023 by her in her petition by aducing oral and documentary evidence. Hence, there is no necessity to discuss regarding sec. 19 of PWDV Act.
 23. With regard to the reliefs as contemplated under Jayalakshmi. K vs Shanmukhappa. H B on 30 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114123177/
8 Sec.18 i.e, the protection orders as well as regarding the possession of mandatory reliefs as contemplated under Sec.20, it becomes just and necessary for the petitioner to establish the same. 
 24. The fact that both petitioner and the respondent are wife and husband is not in dispute. When the petitioner has let in evidence she has stated that subsequent to marriage, she was residing with the respondent in the shared household. After the death of her son, the respondent totally neglected the petitioner and her daughter. Herein, expect oral allegations the petitioner has not furnished any documents to show that the respondent has caused domestic violence against the petitioner. 
 25. While deposing before the court the petitioner has  12  C.Misc. 20/2023 stated that she has also contended that the respondent has used to harass her by neglected to maintain the petitioner and her daughter. Further, on perusal of the pleadings as well as chief affidavit of PW.1, it is clear that the respondent has not caused domestic violence against the petitioner. 
 26. On the other hand, after service of notice, the respondent has not appeared before the court and he placed ex-parte. 
 27. The petitioner examined herself as PW-1 by filing Jayalakshmi. K vs Shanmukhappa. H B on 30 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114123177/
9 affidavit of examination-in-chief. In the said examination-in- chief, she reiterated the averments of the petition. The respondent had not appeared before the court and he is placed ex-parte. Therefore, the cross of PW.1 is taken as nil and also the evidence of the respondent is taken as nil. 
 28. The petitioner in her petition claimed several reliefs. 
On perusal of the materials produced on record, the both parties have not obtained divorce from competent court of law. Further, the petitioner has not proved her case therefore,
 13  C.Misc. 20/2023 the reliefs sought by the petitioner in her petition are cannot be considered. 
 29 . Further, the petitioner is failed to prove the allegations which are made by her in the petition as well as in examination in chief of PW1 in respect of domestic violence caused by the respondent as per Sec. 3 of PWDV Act. 
 30 . The Section 3 in The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 reads as under;
Sec. 3. Definition of domestic violence.--
 For the purposes of this Act, any act, omission or  commission or conduct of the respondent shall  constitute domestic violence in case it.
 (a) harms or injures or endangers the health,
 safety, life, limb or well-being, whether mental or  physical, of the aggrieved person or tends to do so  and includes causing physical abuse, sexual  abuse, verbal and emotional abuse and economic  abuse; or Jayalakshmi. K vs Shanmukhappa. H B on 30 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114123177/
10  (b) harasses, harms, injures or endangers the  aggrieved person with a view to coerce her or any  other person related to her to meet any unlawful  demand for any dowry or other property or  valuable security; or  (c) has the effect of threatening the aggrieved  14  C.Misc. 20/2023  person or any person related to her by any  conduct mentioned in clause (a) or clause (b); or  (d) otherwise injures or causes harm, whether  physical or mental, to the aggrieved person.
 31. On careful perusal of the above section, it is clear that in this case, the respondent has not committed any domestic violence against the petitioner as explained above.
On discussing above, if the respondent has not committed any domestic violence against the petitioner, as contemplated u/sec. 3 of PWDV Act, the petitioner is not entitled for any reliefs as prayed by her in her petition. 
Hence, this court answer these point nos.1 to 4 in the the negative. 
 32. Point No.5: In view of the findings on the above point nos.1 to 4 and the reasons stated therein, this court proceed to pass the following: -
 ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/sec. 12 of the Protection of Women C.Misc. 20/2023 from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is hereby dismissed. 
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in the open court on this the 30 th day of January 2024). 
(Kusuma. V) MMTC-III, Bengaluru.

1. This is petition filed by the petitioner U/sec. 12 of Protection Of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005.
2. By filing this petition the petitioner has sought Jayalakshmi.
K vs Shanmukhappa.

summary.facts:
After two children were born, the petitioner and the respondent made family planning by medical treatment to the petitioner.
In the year 1996 made power of attorney in favour of the petitioner, but not made the sale deed.
In the year 2011, the said house sale deed was registered in the name of Sudha.
Hence, the respondent was placed ex-parte on 13.06.2023.
summary.arguments:
5. The petitioner further submits that after the death of said petitioner's son, the attitude of the respondent totally changed, the respondent used to abuse in filthy language and assaulting the petitioner for the reasons best known to Jayalakshmi.
No where in the petition, the petitioner has stated  10 Jayalakshmi. K vs Shanmukhappa.
25. While deposing before the court the petitioner has  12  C.Misc. 20/2023 stated that she has also contended that the respondent has used to harass her by neglected to maintain the petitioner and her daughter.
summary.issue:
11. Keeping in mind the evidence given by the petitioner it becomes just and necessary to look into whether the orders required by the petitioner various reliefs which are fallen U/sec. 18, 19, 20 and 22 of DV Act can be granted.
14. The points that arise for consideration are:-

 1. Whether the petitioner is entitled for  the Protection Orders as contemplated  under Sec.18 of DV Act?
 2.Whether the petitioner is entitled for Jayalakshmi.

 3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for  monetary relief as contemplated under Sec.20 of DV Act?

 4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for  compensation relief as contemplated  under Sec.22 of DV Act?
 5. What order?
 
The case of the petitioner is that the respondent has given mental and physical harassment by neglecting the petitioner and her daughter.
summary.ANALYSIS:
Further, the respondent had given good education to their children who were born through one Sudha.
But, the respondent has not given proper education to the daughter of the petitioner namely Meenakshi.

Thereafter, the respondent always avoided the petitioner mentally and physically.
Hence he placed ex-parte.
 21.
No doubt, as per Sec.3 of DV Act, if at all the respondent commits any domestic violence as above pleaded is fully established by the petitioner
then definitely the petitioner will be entitled for an order of protection under Sec.18 and for residential orders as per Sec.18 of DV Act and mandatory reliefs as contemplated under Sec.20 of the Act.

 22 . In the case on hand, it is the case of the petitioner that she is residing along with the respondent after the marriage in the shared house, wherein the respondent has given mental and physical torture by not providing basic necessities to the petitioner and her daughter.
In this case, the petitioner has not proved the allegations made  11  C.Misc. 20/2023 by her in her petition by aducing oral and documentary evidence.
When the petitioner has let in evidence she has stated that subsequent to marriage, she was residing with the respondent in the shared household.
After the death of her son, the respondent totally neglected the petitioner and her daughter.

 29 . Further, the petitioner is failed to prove the allegations which are made by her in the petition as well as in examination in chief of PW1 in respect of domestic violence caused by the respondent as per Sec. 3 of PWDV Act.
On discussing above, if the respondent has not committed any domestic violence against the petitioner, as contemplated u/sec. 3 of PWDV Act, the petitioner is not entitled for any reliefs as prayed by her in her petition.
summary.decision:
Hence, this court answer these point nos.1 to 4 in the the negative.
In view of the findings on the above point nos.1 to 4 and the reasons stated therein, this court proceed to pass the following: -
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/sec. 12 of the Protection of Women C.Misc. 20/2023 from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is hereby dismissed.
